observations.classification: Corroborates /root/rig_identity source comparison; no new unique defect count
observations.detail: P16 raw singleton list includes base_clothing and rejects nonzero order. Current validator consults typed EquipmentChannel::singleton_per_location, which excludes BaseClothing; its documentation says ordinary garments use distinct authored orders and conflict logic considers matching order and fit zone. A mechanical full-file diff finds only this replacement (P16 118–121 versus 95e 118–119); the archived test tails were not personally displayed. This is a source and policy difference, not proof of an unintended regression or actual loaded catalog occurrence.
observations.safeguards: Current typed conflict logic distinguishes same location, channel, singleton/order and fit-zone; omission reserves a whole location. P16 and 95e preserve their separate behavior and revision evidence.
observations.open: Supported authored multi-garment cases, strategic/tactical consumers and intended channel compatibility need cross-owner review.

observations.classification: Existing 059 rejected whole-document malformed-occupancy inference, independently corroborated on sampled P16 and 95e paths; no duplicate count
observations.detail: Local occupancy conversion uses .ok(), so a failed typed element can skip the fit/conflict branch. In the selected validate_documents_with_sources route, a non-object root or missing items array adds diagnostics; for a document with an items array the complete ItemCatalogDocument conversion runs and any error is pushed. The positive cap of 128 truncates but does not empty a nonempty diagnostics list, and a nonempty list returns Err. Thus local .ok() alone does not establish that typed-malformed occupancy is accepted by this whole-document route.
observations.safeguards: Typed per-element construction, fit-zone check on successful typed conversion, whole-document typed parse, and positive diagnostic cap are distinct shown checks. No parser or validator was executed.
observations.open: Direct typed DTO construction or deserialization, other admission entry points and real downstream consumers are outside this path and cannot be declared safe or reachable.

observations.classification: Existing 774 rig surface contract, separately corroborated P16 and 95e; conditional open admission/policy question, no new count
observations.detail: The helper requires nonempty spans for armor/clothing, material when spans exist, caps segments, checks nonempty known region chains and directed adjacency, optionally compares to protected body parts, parses SurfaceAnchor and requires coverage positive after f32 narrowing with input at most 1. Public EquipmentSurfaceSpan retains Vec regions and f32 coverage; the type declaration itself does not encode every multi-field policy. No alternate path bypass into a product consumer is established.
observations.safeguards: Caller supplies protected parts and whether material is present; positive_f32_in checks finite, nonzero after narrowing and source maximum. The empty protection set skips surface/protection intersection, which must be assessed in its intended non-armor policy context.
observations.open: All alternative construction/deserialization/consumption routes, valid directed chains, body-part mappings, and non-armor/empty protection semantics require owner decisions. Material presence alone is not proof material is semantically valid.
